findings.reason: The original standalone tiles contain only prose for two independent commuting interfaces. Two small squares materially clarify that Cartan maps change projective to module classes, forgetting changes grading, and transport changes the tower. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, rather than a malformed pre-existing display.
findings.action: Added two commuting tikzcd squares in final Remarks with precise definitions of all arrows and explicit distinction between K and G groups.

correction: Added a Cartan/forgetful square for each specified tower T and a graded Cartan/Hecke-to-KLR transport square; retained every original source byte and all metadata, including status: published.

diagram_math_checks.domains_codomains: c_T^gr: K_0^gr(T) -> G_0^gr(T); zeta_K: K_0^gr(T) -> K_0(T); zeta_G: G_0^gr(T) -> G_0(T); c_T: K_0(T) -> G_0(T).
diagram_math_checks.relation: zeta_G composed with c_T^gr = c_T composed with zeta_K. Both send a graded projective P to its underlying ungraded module class.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Definition lines 46-61 and proof step 1.2; supplier def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map defines both Cartan maps as [P] -> [P]. Finite-dimensional blocks ensure finitely generated projectives are finite-dimensional (F3); taking the restricted sum preserves finite root support.

diagram_math_checks.domains_codomains: T_K: K_0^gr(H^Lambda) -> K_0^gr(R^Lambda); T_G: G_0^gr(H^Lambda) -> G_0^gr(R^Lambda); vertical maps c_H^gr and c_R^gr go from projective to module groups. Rightward transport is restriction along phi_alpha^{-1}: R^Lambda_alpha -> H^Lambda_alpha, not restriction along phi_alpha.
diagram_math_checks.relation: c_R^gr composed with T_K = T_G composed with c_H^gr: both send [P] to the class of the same transported projective considered as a module. T_K and T_G are A-linear isomorphisms, commute with q[M]=[M{1}], and intertwine graded forgetting with their ungraded transports.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Proof step 1.4 explicitly supplies the homogeneous isomorphisms and inverse restrictions, preserves projectives/exactness/shifts, and verifies zero sectors using F6. Restricted sums use finite root support (steps 1.1 and 1.4). Step 2.1 forbids any identification of K with G or arbitrary R with R^Lambda; the squares retain those distinctions.
